body:
The arrangement of land and water

Approximately 71% of the Earth's surface is covered by water and 29% by land. The large continuous landmasses are called continents, while the vast interconnected bodies of saline water are called oceans.

Land and water are distributed unevenly between the hemispheres. The Northern Hemisphere contains a greater proportion of the Earth's land, while the Southern Hemisphere is dominated by oceans. However, water covers more surface area than land even in the Northern Hemisphere.

The 7 continents

The conventional geographical classification recognises 7 continents. In descending order of land area, they are Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe and Australia.

ContinentImportant geographical characteristics
AsiaLargest continent; predominantly north of the Equator; includes the Himalayas
AfricaSecond-largest continent; crossed by the Equator and both tropics
North AmericaConnected to South America through the Isthmus of Panama
South AmericaMostly in the Southern Hemisphere; Andes along its western side
AntarcticaContains the South Pole; largely covered by permanent ice
EuropeWestern part of the Eurasian landmass
AustraliaSmallest continent; entirely in the Southern Hemisphere

Europe and Asia form a continuous landmass called Eurasia. Their separation into 2 continents is based on geographical and historical conventions rather than complete physical separation by an ocean.

One commonly used boundary between Europe and Asia follows the Ural Mountains, Ural River, Caspian Sea, Greater Caucasus region, Black Sea and Turkish Straits. Some conventions differ in their treatment of the Caucasus region.

Australia is a continent, whereas Oceania is a broader geographical region that also includes New Zealand and numerous Pacific islands. Greenland is conventionally classified as the world's largest island rather than a continent.

The 5 oceans

OceanSize rankLocation
Pacific1Between Asia and Australia on one side and the Americas on the other
Atlantic2Between the Americas and Europe-Africa
Indian3Between Africa, Asia and Australia
Southern4Surrounds Antarctica
Arctic5Surrounds the North Pole

All 5 oceans are interconnected. The boundaries between them are conventional geographical divisions rather than physical barriers. The Southern Ocean is commonly defined as the oceanic region south of 60° S.

The Mariana Trench, situated in the western Pacific Ocean, contains the deepest known point in the world's oceans, the Challenger Deep.

Reference lines for locating places

Latitude indicates angular distance north or south of the Equator. Longitude indicates angular distance east or west of the Prime Meridian.

Reference linePosition
Equator0° latitude
Tropic of CancerApproximately 23.5° N
Tropic of CapricornApproximately 23.5° S
Arctic CircleApproximately 66.5° N
Antarctic CircleApproximately 66.5° S
Prime Meridian0° longitude
International Date LineGenerally follows 180° longitude with deviations

The Equator crosses mainland South America, mainland Africa and islands of Southeast Asia. It passes through Ecuador, Colombia, Brazil and Indonesia, among other countries.

Africa is the only continent crossed by the Equator, the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn. Gujarat is crossed by the Tropic of Cancer.

Reading a world map accurately

A physical map shows natural features such as mountains, rivers and oceans. A political map shows countries and administrative boundaries. A thematic map represents a particular subject, such as ocean currents or rainfall.

Every flat world map introduces some distortion because the Earth's curved surface cannot be represented perfectly on a plane. Some projections preserve relative area better than others. On many world maps, the Pacific Ocean appears at both the eastern and western edges, although it is one continuous ocean.

Prelims focus

  • Asia is the largest continent and Australia is the smallest.
  • Pacific is the largest ocean and Arctic is the smallest.
  • Africa is crossed by the Equator and both tropics.
  • The Ural Mountains form part of the conventional Europe-Asia boundary.
  • The Tropic of Cancer passes through Gujarat.
  • Trap: Antarctica is a continent, whereas the Arctic is primarily an ocean surrounded by land.

[References: NCERT, Class 6, The Earth: Our Habitat, 2018–19, Chapters 4–5, pp. 24–35; NCERT, Class 6, Exploring Society: India and Beyond, Chapters 1–2, pp. 7–39; Gujarat State Board of School Textbooks, Geography, Class 11, English-medium 2020 edition, Chapter 5, pp. 30–31; NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information, Ocean Archive System, Southern Ocean definition; Orient BlackSwan School Atlas, World – Physical, p. 81; online sources consulted 26 November 2026.]

title: Understanding the World Map: Continents, Oceans and Reference Lines

body:
Distinguishing geographical water bodies

A sea is generally a subdivision of an ocean, often partly enclosed by land. A gulf or bay is a body of water extending into a landmass. There is no universal size-based rule that distinguishes every gulf from every bay.

An island is a land area surrounded by water. A peninsula projects into water but remains connected to a larger landmass. An archipelago is a group of islands.

Seas and gulfs around Europe and Africa

Water bodyGeographical location
Mediterranean SeaBetween Europe, North Africa and western Asia
Black SeaBetween southeastern Europe and western Asia
Sea of AzovNortheast of the Black Sea
Baltic SeaBetween Scandinavia and northern mainland Europe
North SeaBetween Great Britain, Scandinavia and mainland Europe
Adriatic SeaBetween Italy and the western Balkan Peninsula
Aegean SeaBetween Greece and Türkiye
Red SeaBetween northeastern Africa and the Arabian Peninsula
Gulf of GuineaAtlantic coast of western Africa
Gulf of AdenBetween Yemen and the Horn of Africa
Persian GulfBetween Iran and the Arabian Peninsula
Gulf of OmanBetween Iran and Oman, east of the Strait of Hormuz

Countries bordering important enclosed seas

The Black Sea has 6 coastal countries: Türkiye, Bulgaria, Romania, Ukraine, Russia and Georgia. The Caspian Sea has 5 coastal countries: Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran and Azerbaijan.

The Red Sea lies between Egypt, Sudan, Eritrea and Djibouti on its African side and Saudi Arabia and Yemen on its Arabian side. Its northern extensions include the Gulf of Suez and the Gulf of Aqaba. Jordan and Israel have coastlines along the Gulf of Aqaba.

The Indian Ocean and the waters of eastern Asia

Water bodyGeographical location
Arabian SeaWest of India
Bay of BengalEast of India
Andaman SeaEast of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands
South China SeaSouth of China, east of Vietnam and west of the Philippines
East China SeaEast of China, between China and the Japanese island chain
Yellow SeaBetween China and the Korean Peninsula
Sea of JapanBetween Japan, the Korean Peninsula and the Russian Far East
Sea of OkhotskBetween northeastern Asia and the Kuril island chain
Bering SeaBetween Alaska and northeastern Russia
Coral SeaNortheast of Australia
Tasman SeaBetween Australia and New Zealand

Water bodies around the Americas

Water bodyLocation
Caribbean SeaEast of Central America and north of South America
Gulf of MexicoBetween the United States, Mexico and Cuba
Hudson BayNortheastern Canada
Gulf of CaliforniaBetween the Baja California Peninsula and mainland Mexico

Important islands and peninsulas

FeatureTypeLocation
GreenlandIslandBetween the Arctic and North Atlantic oceans
MadagascarIslandOff southeastern Africa
Sri LankaIslandSouth of India
BorneoIslandMaritime Southeast Asia
SumatraIslandWestern Indonesia
New GuineaIslandNorth of Australia
ArabianPeninsulaBetween the Red Sea and Persian Gulf region
IberianPeninsulaSouthwestern Europe
ScandinavianPeninsulaNorthern Europe
KoreanPeninsulaEastern Asia
KamchatkaPeninsulaRussian Far East
SinaiPeninsulaEgypt, between the gulfs of Suez and Aqaba

Borneo is shared by Indonesia, Malaysia and Brunei. New Guinea is shared by Indonesia and Papua New Guinea. Greenland is geographically part of North America, although it is politically associated with Denmark.

Inland water bodies with important geographical names

The name of a water body does not necessarily determine its geographical classification. The Caspian Sea, Aral Sea and Dead Sea are inland water bodies rather than subdivisions of an open ocean.

Water bodyImportant distinction
Caspian SeaWorld's largest inland body of water by surface area
Aral SeaBetween Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan; historically fed by the Amu Darya and Syr Darya
Dead SeaHighly saline lake in the Jordan Rift Valley
Lake BaikalRussia; world's deepest lake
Lake VictoriaShared by Tanzania, Uganda and Kenya
Lake TanganyikaDeep freshwater lake in the East African Rift region
Lake SuperiorLargest freshwater lake by surface area when the Great Lakes are counted individually
Lake TiticacaAndean highlands between Peru and Bolivia

Gujarat's maritime geography

Gujarat faces the Arabian Sea. The Gulf of Kachchh lies between the Kachchh region and the Saurashtra Peninsula, while the Gulf of Khambhat lies between eastern Saurashtra and mainland Gujarat.

Deendayal Port, commonly associated with Kandla, is situated in the Gulf of Kachchh region. The Narmada and Tapi rivers discharge into the Gulf of Khambhat.

Prelims focus

  • The Black Sea has 6 coastal countries; the Caspian Sea has 5.
  • The Yellow Sea separates China from the Korean Peninsula.
  • The Tasman Sea lies between Australia and New Zealand.
  • Madagascar lies southeast of mainland Africa.
  • The Caspian Sea is the largest inland water body by surface area.
  • Trap: The Caspian Sea and Dead Sea are inland lakes despite their names.

[References: NCERT, Class 6, Exploring Society: India and Beyond, Chapter 2, pp. 27–39; NCERT, Class 7, Our Environment, 2018–19, Chapter 5, pp. 30–38; United Nations Geospatial, Map of the World, July 2026 revision; Orient BlackSwan School Atlas, World – Physical, p. 81 and regional physical maps; Deendayal Port Authority, Environmental Monitoring Report, June–July 2026, Map 1, p. 8; online sources consulted 26 November 2026.]

body:
What is a strait?

A strait is a naturally formed narrow water passage connecting larger bodies of water and separating neighbouring land areas.

Straits are important for geographical identification because each can be understood through 2 relationships: the water bodies it connects and the land areas it separates. A narrow passage through which substantial maritime traffic passes is often described as a maritime chokepoint.

A strait differs from an isthmus. An isthmus is a narrow strip of land connecting larger land areas and separating water bodies.

Straits of Europe and western Asia

StraitConnectsSeparates
GibraltarAtlantic Ocean and Mediterranean SeaSpain and Morocco
BosporusBlack Sea and Sea of MarmaraEuropean and Asian parts of Türkiye
DardanellesSea of Marmara and Aegean SeaGallipoli Peninsula and Asian Türkiye
KerchBlack Sea and Sea of AzovCrimean and Taman peninsulas
DoverEnglish Channel and North SeaGreat Britain and France
HormuzPersian Gulf and Gulf of OmanIran and Oman's Musandam Peninsula
Bab el-MandebRed Sea and Gulf of AdenArabian Peninsula and Horn of Africa

The Turkish Straits

The Bosporus and Dardanelles are collectively called the Turkish Straits. Both are located in Türkiye, with the Sea of Marmara between them.

From north to south, the correct geographical sequence is the Black Sea, Bosporus, Sea of Marmara, Dardanelles and Aegean Sea. The Aegean Sea forms part of the Mediterranean system.

The Persian Gulf and Hormuz

Bahrain, Qatar and Kuwait lie within the Persian Gulf region. Ships leaving their Persian Gulf ports for the open Indian Ocean normally pass through the Strait of Hormuz. The strait opens into the Gulf of Oman, which connects to the Arabian Sea.

Straits of southern and eastern Asia

StraitWater connectionLand areas
PalkBay of Bengal and Palk BayIndia and Sri Lanka
MalaccaAndaman Sea towards the South China Sea through the Singapore StraitMalay Peninsula and Sumatra
SundaJava Sea and Indian OceanSumatra and Java
LombokIndian Ocean and Bali SeaBali and Lombok
TaiwanEast China Sea and South China Sea regionMainland China and Taiwan
LuzonSouth China Sea and Philippine SeaTaiwan and Luzon region
KoreaEast China Sea region and Sea of JapanKorean Peninsula and Japan

The Strait of Malacca is a major link between the Indian Ocean and western Pacific maritime networks. The Sunda and Lombok straits lie farther south within the Indonesian archipelago.

The Palk Strait and Palk Bay lie between southeastern India and northern Sri Lanka. Adam's Bridge, a chain of shallow shoals, separates the Palk Bay region from the Gulf of Mannar to the south.

Other important world passages

PassageWater connectionLocation
Bering StraitBering Sea and Chukchi SeaRussia and Alaska, United States
Strait of MagellanAtlantic and Pacific oceansMainland southern South America and Tierra del Fuego
Drake PassageSouthern Atlantic-Pacific regionSouth America and Antarctica
Bass StraitIndian Ocean and Tasman SeaMainland Australia and Tasmania
Torres StraitCoral Sea and Arafura SeaAustralia and New Guinea
Mozambique ChannelWestern Indian OceanMozambique and Madagascar

The Bering Strait separates North America from Asia and provides a connection between the Pacific and Arctic ocean systems.

The Strait of Magellan and Drake Passage are both near the southern end of South America, but their geographical positions differ. The former passes between mainland South America and Tierra del Fuego, while the latter lies farther south between South America and Antarctica.

Prelims focus

  • Gibraltar connects the Atlantic Ocean and Mediterranean Sea.
  • Hormuz connects the Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman.
  • Bab el-Mandeb connects the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden.
  • Malacca separates the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra.
  • Bering Strait separates Russia and Alaska.
  • Trap: Bosporus opens into the Black Sea; Dardanelles opens into the Aegean Sea.

[References: NCERT, Class 6, The Earth: Our Habitat, 2018–19, Chapter 5, Figure 5.2, p. 33; U.S. Energy Information Administration, World Oil Transit Chokepoints, updated 3 March 2026, geographical sections on Hormuz, Malacca, Bab el-Mandeb and the Turkish Straits; United Nations Geospatial, Map of the World, July 2026 revision; Orient BlackSwan School Atlas, regional physical maps; PSC Chronicles, Important Straits of the World; online sources consulted 26 November 2026.]
